title: Extension of a trait line section from integral special-fibre generic germs
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:Y\to S$ be flat and of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume its special fibre $Y_k$ is reduced and pure of dimension one, meaning every irreducible component has dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $U\subseteq Y$ be an open containing the generic fibre $Y_K$, and let $s_U\in\Gamma(U,M|_U)$. For every generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $Y_k$, assume the germ of $s_U|_{Y_K}$ in $M_\eta[1/\pi]$ belongs to the image of $M_\eta$. Then there is a unique $s\in\Gamma(Y,M)$ with $s|_U=s_U$. Moreover restriction $\Gamma(V,M)\to\Gamma(V\cap Y_K,M)$ is injective for every open $V\subseteq Y$. There exists an open $W\supseteq U$ containing every generic point of $Y_k$ on which the integral germs and $s_U$ agree and glue to a section; every $y\notin W$ has $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\geq2$ and $\operatorname{depth}M_y\geq2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. No normality, integrality, properness, smoothness, nodal condition, marking, or connectedness of $Y$ is assumed. The empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog), combined with algebra.tex lemma-criterion-reduced and lemma-apply-grothendieck; agent generic-germ spreading and depth argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 1 and 8--10. The tag alone assumes the depth condition, whereas this statement derives it from the reduced curve special fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-curve-line-depth] with $X=Y$ and $m=1$ (and $m=0$ for the structure sheaf). Thus $Y$ is Noetherian, multiplication by $\pi$ on every stalk of $M$ is injective, and at closed points of $Y_k$ both required depths are at least two. We need injectivity on arbitrary opens, which we check next rather than applying this finite-type lemma to an arbitrary open.

On an affine open $T$, the generic part is $D(\pi)$ and restriction is localization, as in [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-affine-ring-models]. If $t\in\Gamma(T,M)$ vanishes there, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization] gives $\pi^n t=0$. At each point $x\in T$, injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$ on $M_x$ gives $t_x=0$. Equality of germs means equality on some neighbourhood by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives $t=0$. Covering any open $V$ by affine opens proves the asserted injectivity on $V$; taking a difference proves equality detection for any pair of sections.

Fix a generic point $\eta$ of $Y_k$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $T$ on which $M$ is trivial, using [def-sc-invertible-module]. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization] writes $s_U|_{T_K}=a/\pi^n$ with $a\in\Gamma(T,M)$. The hypothesis gives $b_\eta\in M_\eta$ mapping to this germ. Thus $\pi^n b_\eta=a_\eta$ in $M_\eta[1/\pi]$, hence in $M_\eta$ by Step 1: a localization equality is killed by some power of $\pi$, and that power acts injectively. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], represent $b_\eta$ by a section $b$ near $\eta$ and shrink to an open $T_\eta\subseteq T$ where $\pi^n b=a$. On $(T_\eta)_K$, $\pi$ is a unit, so $b=s_U$. This explicitly spreads the prescribed integral germ.

source.place: Tags 01HV and 01IA; sheaves.tex section-stalks; agent spreading of the integral germ (Tag 0078)

proof.text: Put $W=U\cup\bigcup_\eta T_\eta$. On $T_\eta\cap U$ the sections $b$ and $s_U$ agree after restriction to the generic fibre, so agree by Step 2. The same argument on $T_\eta\cap T_{\eta\prime}$ proves pairwise compatibility, without assuming the intersections affine. The sheaf gluing axiom gives $s_W\in\Gamma(W,M)$ with these restrictions. It has the chosen integral germs at every $\eta$. The integral lifts themselves are unique by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 006T, definition-sheaf, and Tag 0077, definition-sheaf-modules; agent assembly of the preceding spreading and injectivity arguments

proof.text: Every $y\notin W$ lies in $Y_k$ and is not a generic point of a component. Such a point is closed in $Y_k$: its closure $Z$ is a proper irreducible closed subset of a component $C$; if it had a distinct specialization $z$, then $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq Z\subsetneq C$ would be a chain of length two, contradicting $\dim C=1$. Here schemes are $T_0$, so the first inclusion is strict. This uses precisely the chain definition in [def-weil-pure-dimension] and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], not smoothness or normality. Step 1 therefore gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\ge2$ and $\operatorname{depth}M_y\ge2$ at every point outside $W$.

source.place: Tag 0337 via Step 1; elementary chain-of-irreducible-closed-subsets argument for the boundary; scheme T_0 property (Tag 01IS, schemes.tex lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text: Cover $Y$ by affine opens $T$ trivializing $M$, and write $s_W|_{T\cap W}=c_T e_T$ in the chosen basis [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-sbc-depth-two-hartogs-restriction] to $L=T$, $N=\mathcal O_T$ and the open $T\cap W$. The scheme $T$ is locally Noetherian by Step 1; $\mathcal O_T$ is quasi-coherent; its sections on every affine open and its stalks are free of rank one over their own rings, hence finite. Its boundary stalks have depth at least two by Step 5. The restriction unit is an isomorphism, so evaluating it on $T$ extends $c_T$ uniquely to $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Multiply by $e_T$. These local sections agree on overlaps by Step 2, since their generic restrictions are $s_U|_{Y_K}$, and hence glue to $s\in\Gamma(Y,M)$. On $U$ this section and $s_U$ agree by the same injectivity; any two extensions agree on $Y_K$ and hence on $Y$. If $Y$ or $Y_k$ is empty the construction has no missing germs or boundary and the same argument applies.
